answers.answer: In a 3-player Census, the tied leaders gain nothing; the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: “a tied lead gives no coin”; “In a 2-player game the last player never pays”.

answers.answer: No. Draw at most the two free Market spaces (and you may draw fewer). Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers: “up to the allowance… limited by free Market spaces”; “Unused Market Followers remain between rounds”.

answers.answer: You may partially fill an action across rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied (except Town Hall, where one space suffices). A fully activated action may be saved. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Town Hall sends its selected Followers to Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Planning/Actions: “fill an action gradually”; “An activation can be saved”; ordinary-action Followers “return… to your bag”.

answers.answer: Players take one activated action or pass, in clockwise order from Start Player, repeatedly. Passing ends your participation for that Action Phase; unused activations retain their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions: “one activated action or passing”; “Passing ends your participation”; unused activations “keep their Followers on the board”.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the depicted good.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Farm House: “Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.”

answers.answer: Village recruits one Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advances that profession’s track one space. Boatman gives depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first player at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives a Place Tile, with the first advance restricted to category I and later advances allowing I or II.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment section.

answers.answer: No. A newly acquired Technology can be used only after you pass, so it cannot help execute another action that round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology can replace any profession except Monk; no more than one at a Place, and none at a Place requiring only one Follower. Technology is permanent and cannot be moved.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Craftsman; Technology section.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance allows category I only; every later advance allows category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Trader; Setup, item 3.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and awards its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track one space. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag, with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight does not increase allowance above 7 at that step; once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table — University, Castle, Monastery; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight for an ordinary action. No Knight or Technology may replace a required Monk. No Monk substitution may replace the exact profession required on a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Monks section; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds section.

answers.answer: A Ship moves the Merchant one adjacent Waterway connection; a Wagon moves one adjacent Road connection. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if there are several. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods section.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player’s station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building section.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point (move one space on the Development Track). Moving onto or past a coin space collects its coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching/passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Scriptorium; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Town Hall can be activated with one or two eligible Followers and can send one or both in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send them to free Beneficial Deed spaces matching their exact professions; take each space’s depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins, or for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed’s final space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Town Hall; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during that round’s Action Phase; it takes effect before the Event Phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The first Hour Glass tile is Pilgrimage.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass and Event; Setup, item 4; Events table — Pilgrimage.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualify as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you have no food, you owe 5 coins; if unable to pay those coins, torture applies for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Events — Harvest.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar returns to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable; its track marker does not move back. If Plague draws your marked starting Trader, keep it, lose no Follower, and do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Events — Plague.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then cover each of the two missing coins with one eligible item per missing coin: a built or unbuilt station, an eligible random neutral Follower from your bag, one Development Point, one good, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Marked starting Followers cannot be sacrificed; redraw them until an eligible neutral Follower is drawn. A Development Point moves one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game; only lost Development Points can be regained.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy).

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still give a reward. It becomes available again when the required tile returns to stock, subject to usual requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies.

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations gives the bonus Citizen to nobody. Goods score grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 points each. Built stations plus collected Citizens score (stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Ties go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put the starting Followers on your Market, Merchant in Orléans, one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track; keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes the Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup, items 2 and final paragraph.

answers.answer: Set up the shared boards; sort neutral Followers by profession into their board buildings, Technology into its supply, coins nearby. Put 13 Citizens on marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Separate Place Tiles into category I and II stacks. For four players, fill every eligible Road/Waterway goods space with one face-up good; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup, items 1, 3, and 5; fewer players note says 4-player games fill every space.

answers.answer: For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; randomly remove 6 goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each of the first four professions; 6 of each Knight, Scholar, and Monk; randomly remove 12 goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Setup — Fewer players table and preceding sentence.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table — required professions.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table — required professions.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall accepts 1 or 2 eligible Followers; their exact professions are not specified by a printed Town Hall profession requirement, but the marked starting Followers are excluded.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Scriptorium and Town Hall; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Yes. Declining two draws lets you move two Followers from Action Spaces back to your Market. You may not move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers.

answers.answer: Order: Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token left. Planning starts simultaneously; announce completion, and if order matters plan clockwise from Start Player. Order-sensitive Event payments/resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, phases 1–7.

answers.answer: Do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, including its event; then score.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: The uniquely ahead player on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in bags.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: compare markers regardless of Farmer tiles currently in bags.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events — Income.

answers.answer: Eight goods mean two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins; goods types do not change the calculation. If unable to pay, torture applies for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Events — Taxes: count all goods, 1 coin per complete group of 3, round down.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, since Trading Day pays 1 per built Trading Station; unbuilt stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Events — Trading Day; Building says only built stations count for income.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; brocade from Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used if its particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table and following sentence.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are not allowed.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Pharmacy.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight; move along one Road to an adjacent town and collect one good if available.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to usual placement constraints. The first Technology may be placed on the Laboratory itself if legal, including the first-tile Farmer restriction; later Technology may also be placed there if no Technology is already there and other placement rules are met.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Laboratory; Technology section.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on the Bathhouse. Return the third drawn tile and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Bathhouse.

answers.answer: Place the one tile that can legally go on an allowed Action Space. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Bathhouse: “If you can legally place only one or none…”

answers.answer: It may be executed later in the same Action Phase if you have not passed: after Bathhouse places the needed Follower, the other Place is activated, and actions may be taken in freely chosen order.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse says tiles are immediately placed on appropriate Action Spaces; Turn Structure — Actions says choose actions’ order freely and passing ends participation.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, it protects against a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague. During Phase 6, return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering the event.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Sacristy.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5, before the Phase 6 event resolution; Sacristy’s protection applies during Phase 6, so it cannot bypass that restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass/Pilgrimage and Event; Sacristy entry.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — School.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deeds require the exact depicted professions, and substitutions cannot replace them. This remains true when using Gunpowder Tower; it provides an alternate way to send Followers to Deeds, but Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Gunpowder Tower entry.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. In Planning move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, in Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent; Deed spaces still require exact professions.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied last players pay nothing because tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census.

answers.answer: The unique leader in built Trading Stations receives the set-aside Citizen before scoring, after the full final round. It counts as a collected Citizen for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most takes set-aside Citizen before scoring; Citizens included in scoring formula.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then place that Pilgrimage on top, so round 1 is Pilgrimage. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup, item 4; Turn Structure — Hour Glass.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table — Coins.

answers.answer: Initial Development Status is 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup, item 2.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy).

answers.answer: You may choose the order of your actions freely; neither printed order nor order filled is required.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions: “Choose your actions’ order freely.”

answers.answer: The summary says the new Place may be used under normal timing rules and describes Herb Garden/School as ongoing abilities with no activation. It does not explicitly specify whether a passive ability acquired during Phase 5 applies immediately in that same phase.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Trader says new Place may be used under normal timing rules; Place table says School and Herb Garden give ongoing abilities.

answers.answer: You may send just one; Town Hall permits sending one or both.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: “send one or both”.

answers.answer: You may leave the good there. Movement permits taking one good, and does not require taking it.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good from that connection”.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the second on a later action turn during the same Action Phase before passing; Town Hall’s two Followers may be resolved in the same or separate actions.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Town Hall may send its two Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before passing.
